# Billing System Migration Rollout Plan
## 40,000 Users — Old and New Systems Running in Parallel

## Overview

This plan migrates 40,000 existing users from the legacy billing system to the new billing system in four named phases, using dual-running (both systems live simultaneously) to allow verification and safe rollback at each stage. The old billing system remains fully operational — including for billing runs, support, and reconciliation — throughout all migration phases and is only considered for retirement after a dedicated post-migration stabilization phase.

---

## Phase 1: Canary (0.25% — 100 users)

**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed full integration testing in staging, including parallel invoice-generation reconciliation against the old system for at least 30 consecutive days with zero unexplained discrepancies; rollback tooling has been tested end-to-end; on-call rotation is staffed.

**Scope:** ~100 internal/employee accounts and consenting low-risk external users (e.g., free-tier or low-transaction-volume accounts), selected to minimize customer impact if issues arise.

**Duration:** 1–2 weeks minimum.

**Activities:**
- Migrate account, payment method, and subscription data for the cohort.
- Run both systems in parallel per user: new system becomes source of truth for that user's billing events, old system continues shadow-processing (read-only reconciliation) for cross-checking.
- Daily manual reconciliation review.

**Exit criterion:** Invoice accuracy ≥ 99.9%, no data-integrity incidents, support ticket volume from cohort within normal baseline.

---

## Phase 2: Early Adopters (5% — 2,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 exit criteria met and signed off by engineering + finance leads; automated reconciliation dashboard operational (no longer manual-only); at least 7 days elapsed post-Phase 1 with no regression.

**Scope:** ~2,000 users, stratified sample across customer segments (plan tiers, geographies, payment methods) to surface edge cases (e.g., proration, tax jurisdictions, currency handling, dunning/failed-payment flows) before wider exposure.

**Duration:** 2–3 weeks.

**Activities:**
- Enable customer-facing new billing UI/emails for cohort only.
- Automated nightly reconciliation between old and new systems for migrated accounts.
- Collect explicit support/CSAT feedback from this cohort.

**Exit criterion:** Metrics below stay within thresholds for 14 consecutive days; no P1/P2 incidents attributable to new system.

---

## Phase 3: General Availability Ramp (65% — 26,000 users, migrated in weekly sub-batches of ~10–15%)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 exit criteria met; payment gateway and tax-provider partners have confirmed production readiness at scale; customer support team trained and staffed for expected ticket volume increase; automated rollback-per-account tooling validated (ability to revert an individual account to the old system without a full-batch rollback).

**Scope:** Remaining users excluding the final cohort (see Phase 4), migrated in weekly waves (e.g., 10% → 15% → 20% → 20% cumulative) rather than as a single cutover, with a go/no-go checkpoint before each sub-batch.

**Duration:** 6–8 weeks.

**Activities:**
- Weekly sub-batch migration with automated data-parity checks pre- and post-migration per account.
- Old system continues running in parallel as shadow processor for all migrated accounts through this phase (not decommissioned).
- Load and performance testing at each doubling of migrated volume.

**Exit criterion:** Cumulative error and complaint metrics remain within threshold across all sub-batches; no unresolved P1 incidents.

---

## Phase 4: Final Cutover Batch (29.75% — ~11,900 users, remaining/highest-risk accounts)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 3 fully complete with 30 consecutive days of stable metrics; all known edge-case categories (enterprise contracts, custom pricing, legacy payment methods, multi-entity billing) have each been validated with at least one successful migrated exemplar account; finance has completed a full audit reconciliation of Phases 1–3 migrated accounts.

**Scope:** Remaining users, typically the highest-complexity accounts (enterprise contracts, custom billing terms, long-tenured legacy configurations) deliberately migrated last since they carry the most integration risk.

**Duration:** 4–6 weeks, in smaller sub-batches given higher per-account complexity.

**Activities:**
- White-glove migration process for complex/enterprise accounts, including account-manager notification.
- Full parallel run maintained; old system remains the system of record for any account pending final verification.

**Exit criterion:** All 40,000 users successfully migrated and reconciled; old system verified to have zero active billing dependencies.

---

## Post-Migration: Old System Retirement (separate phase, not part of migration phases above)

**Explicitly not bundled with Phase 4.** Only after Phase 4 completes and a minimum 60-day parallel-run stabilization/audit window has passed with no reconciliation discrepancies does the organization begin a *separate* decommissioning phase for the old billing system (read-only archival period first, then disablement, then decommission). This separation is intentional: the final batch of migrated users must have a fully operational fallback system available during and immediately after their cutover.

---

## Key Metrics and Halt Threshold

Tracked continuously via automated dashboard from Phase 1 onward:
- Invoice/charge accuracy rate (migrated vs. expected)
- Payment failure rate delta (new system vs. historical old-system baseline)
- Reconciliation discrepancy count between old and new systems
- Support ticket volume and severity for migrated cohorts
- API/system error rate for new billing system

**Halt condition:** If the billing discrepancy rate (invoices with incorrect amount, duplicate charge, or missed charge) among migrated accounts exceeds **0.5% in any rolling 24-hour window**, the rollout is immediately halted, no further accounts are migrated into the next batch/phase, and the incident response and rollback process is triggered for the affected accounts.

Additional stop-the-line triggers (any one is sufficient to pause and convene a go/no-go review):
- Payment failure rate for migrated accounts exceeds baseline old-system failure rate by more than 1.5x over a rolling 48-hour window.
- Any P1 data-integrity incident (e.g., wrong customer charged, PCI/PII exposure).

---

## Risks

RISK: Payment gateway/tax-provider integration behaves differently under new system at scale | Load-test with production-scale synthetic traffic and run partner certification before Phase 3; keep old system as live fallback | Engineering Lead (Billing Platform)
RISK: Data mapping errors during migration cause incorrect charges to customers | Automated pre/post-migration parity checks on every account plus per-account rollback capability | Data Migration Lead
RISK: Customer support overwhelmed by ticket volume during ramp phases | Staff and train support ahead of each phase based on projected volume; throttle batch size if ticket volume exceeds baseline by 2x | Customer Support Manager
RISK: Complex enterprise/custom-billing accounts fail migration due to unhandled edge cases | Migrate highest-complexity accounts last (Phase 4) only after all edge-case categories validated with exemplar accounts | Finance Systems Lead
RISK: Premature decommissioning of old system leaves no fallback for final cutover batch | Enforce mandatory 60-day parallel-run stabilization period after Phase 4 before any decommission activity begins | VP Engineering / Billing Program Owner

PHASES: 4
